source.title: Beyond Single Concept Vector: Modeling Concept Subspace in LLMs with Gaussian Distribution
source.authors: Hai-Yan Zhao; Heng Zhao; Bo Shen; Ali Payani; Fan Yang; Meng-Nan Du

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates Gaussian concept subspaces from linear-probe vectors in LLMs, but does not test superposition, feature-capacity competition, polysemanticity, or SAE features. Toy Models of Superposition appears in the references only.
record.gate_note: The paper's concept-vector similarity and accuracy results concern its GCS representation method, not whether sparse features overlap because of limited dimensions. Its emotion-steering experiment deliberately induces joyful output, so it is not evidence about naturally occurring feature geometry. Results from cited work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes Gaussian Concept Subspace (GCS) from repeated linear probes on Llama-2-7B/13B and Gemma-7B and evaluates its own method (similarity, accuracy, hierarchy plausibility, steering). It does not measure feature count vs. dimension, sparsity, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or whether features are 1-D vs multi-dimensional. Its 'multidimensional subspace' is a distribution over probe-weight vectors arising from data resampling, assumed rather than tested as a feature geometry. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: authors conclude GCS is faithful (sampled vectors similar to observed and comparably or more accurate), plausible (recovers concept hierarchies), and that 1σ GCS vectors balance steering effect and fluency in emotion steering.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes Gaussian Concept Subspace from repeated linear-probe classifiers; it does not reproduce or apply the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports layerwise changes in vector similarity and evaluates samples at different distances from the GCS mean (1σ–5σ); its steering results also vary with sampling distance and steering strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe vectors sampled within 1σ of a Gaussian fit to 1,000 resampled linear-probe vectors have cosine similarity >0.93 to each other and ~0.88–0.93 to observed vectors, with comparable or better classification accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Llama-2 and Gemma-7B, a Gaussian over repeated linear-probe vectors yields concept vectors with similar geometry and predictive performance to individually trained probes.

record.problems: The study does not measure feature sparsity, feature count relative to dimensions, neuron polysemanticity, or superposition. It uses GPT-4o-generated concept data; the authors note that GPT-4o evaluations of generated text may be inaccurate. The cited accuracy figures are not numerically reported in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's other GCS evaluations, including concept-hierarchy visualizations and induced emotion-steering outcomes, do not measure any claim version. Emotion steering is intentionally induced. No additional claim-relevant rows were omitted.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity, or feature-vs-dimension geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All: no neuron distribution or dictionary/SAE recovery measured.
Whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional; the paper's subspace is a Gaussian over probe vectors with diagonal covariance, motivated by assumption, not tested against 1-D features.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's 'multidimensional concept subspace' framing could superficially seem to bear on V6, but the variability modelled is probe-training variance across data resamples, not a multi-dimensional feature in activations; no comparison against a 1-D representation's adequacy is made. Steering is deliberately induced and evaluates the method.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparse-feature overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Feature distribution across neurons and recovery of sparse LLM features with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B, Gemma-7B, and Llama-2-13B (aggregate reported)
rows.stage_stated: Llama-2-7B chat and Llama-2-13B chat; Gemma-7B stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared cosine similarities among observed probe vectors, among GCS-sampled vectors, and across the two sets.

conditions.value: Penultimate-layer comparison; layerwise plots also reported

rows.baseline: Observed-vector similarities are reported as ranging approximately from 0.8 to 0.9.
rows.value: Sampled-vector similarities are reported as larger than 0.93; observed-to-sampled similarities typically range from 0.88 to 0.93.
rows.note: These are aggregate textual ranges across the three models; the paper says the patterns are consistent across them. They measure similarity of probe-derived concept vectors, not superposition or feature overlap.
rows.check: Measures cosine similarity among probe vectors from the authors' own GCS method; this is an evaluation of the study's method, not a measure of superposition or feature dimensionality. Arguably should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B, Gemma-7B, and Llama-2-13B (aggregate reported)
rows.stage_stated: Llama-2-7B chat and Llama-2-13B chat; Gemma-7B stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated observed and sampled concept vectors on concept-classification datasets.

conditions.value: Observed vectors on an 8,000-description test set; sampled vectors on the 10,000-sample dataset

rows.baseline: Observed-vector accuracy; exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.value: Sampled vectors usually achieve comparable or better accuracy, particularly at 1σ and 2σ; exact values are shown in Figure 3.
rows.note: The text summarizes the figure without giving exact accuracies. This concerns GCS concept-vector performance and does not test the listed superposition versions.
rows.check: Classification accuracy of GCS-sampled vs observed probe vectors; evaluates the study's own method, values only in Figure 3. Not a claim-relevant row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
